Temperature: after ovulation, progesterone raises your resting temperature by about 0.2–0.5 °C until your next period. When 3 readings in a row are higher than the 6 before them, and the third is at least 0.2 °C above that level (the coverline), ovulation is confirmed. It most likely happened the day before the first high reading. The rise comes after ovulation: it confirms ovulation but cannot announce it. Ondea uses it to learn your ovulation day for the next cycles.

Cervical mucus: the first sign of mucus opens the fertile window. The peak day (P) is the last day of the best-quality mucus, and ovulation usually happens within a day of it. Following the symptothermal double check, the fertile phase only ends when both signs agree: the temperature rise is confirmed and 3 days have passed since the peak.

Before any sign appears, the fertile window is predicted from your past confirmed ovulations, your usual ovulation day, or your cycle length. It covers the 5 days before ovulation, ovulation day and the day after. It opens 5 days before your earliest recent ovulation, because the fertile window changes from cycle to cycle. Sperm can survive up to 5 days, and the egg about 1 day.

resources.string: In research charts, basal temperature has two levels. This is the typical shape:
Period: the cycle starts on the first day of bleeding. The temperature is low.
Follicular phase: estrogen rises. The temperature stays low. The mucus changes from dry to sticky, creamy, then egg white.
Ovulation: most often the last low day before the rise. The mucus peak is usually within a day of it.
Luteal phase: progesterone raises the temperature by about 0.2–0.5 °C for 10 to 16 days, until the next period.
Typical basal temperature curve: low until ovulation, then higher until the next period.
Ondea helps you understand your cycle with the symptothermal method: your morning temperature and your body signs. Your data stays on this phone, encrypted. No account, no ads, no tracking.

After ovulation, your temperature goes up and stays higher until your next period. When 3 readings in a row are above the 6 before them, the rise is confirmed and Ondea marks the ovulation.

At first, Ondea estimates your fertile days from what you enter in the setup. Day by day, your temperature and mucus move the estimate. After each cycle, Ondea learns your own pattern and tells you when it differs from your settings.
Ondea is not a contraceptive and not a medical device.

The change after ovulation is small: about 0.3 to 0.7 °C. To see it, the readings must be precise and taken the same way every day.
A basal thermometer with 2 decimals (for example 36.47 °C). A fever thermometer is not precise enough.
Every morning at about the same time (within an hour), right after you wake up: before you get up, talk, eat or drink.
After at least 3 hours of sleep. Always at the same place: mouth, vagina or rectum.
